Q: Why does std::print segfaults when using a string parameter? A:

Is this some sort of undefined behavior, or is it a bug in this particular compiler?

Yes, this is definitely a well-formed program and so a compiler bug/issue or compiler explorer backend issue like this.

From std::println's documentation, the call std::println("hello from {}", "me"); is equivalent to:

std::println(stdout, "hello from {}", "me");

which itself is equivalent to:

std::print(stdout, "{}\n", std::format("hello from {}", "me"));

both of which should themselves result in a well-formed program.

Note

There have been some similar old bug reports(with sigbus) like this(for compiler explorer) in the past, for example C++: ARM64 gcc trunk and 15.1 "Execute the code" fails with sigbus. This may or may not be related to these old issue(s) which btw are still open.

Q: Failure to Detect <img> Tags When Bulk Downloading Copyright-Free Images A:

Some websites block direct downloads to protect their content. If you get a 403 Forbidden error even with the right link, it means that specific site is blocking the request.

Q: Python Polars Read Zipped CSV A:

IMO one useful approach for zipfiles that I haven't seen discussed in detail is to learn about fsspec url-chaining
https://filesystem-spec.readthedocs.io/en/latest/features.html#url-chaining

The example below works far quicker than any of the other more explicit attempts I've made to open the zip file. It's particularly good for online datasets

import polars as pl
df = pl.read_csv("zip://path/to/csv.csv::https://www.my_data.com/downloads/zipped_dataset",infer_schema=False)
